text:
maya: Quick broadcast: starting 2025-04-07 were rolling out artifact signing for all SDK releases and adding provenance metadata to docs samples. This covers Py/JS/Go packages and the embedded examples we publish. :loudspeaker:
kenji: Can you summarize whats changing for folks who just pip/npm install during dev?
maya: TL;DR: installers will prefer signed artifacts. During the transition well accept unsigned but emit a warning. Full verification becomes mandatory on 2025-05-31.
kenji: Any docs or runbooks we can link?
maya: Draft RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/sdk-artifact-provenance (please review). Ill publish a step-by-step guide in docs next week.
olivia-k: For Private deployments, does this force customers to import a Redwood key?
maya: Yes, for offline/private installs customers must import our verification key or use the provided verification helper. Well ship an installable trust bundle + one-line import script.
security-bot: Security note: well generate SBOMs for each release and scan artifacts for unexpected native deps. This lowers supply-chain risk and helps audit.
jason: What about CI and pinned dependencies? We have pinned wheels in some pipelines.
maya: Were adding a 60-day grace window for pinned artifacts. CI can opt-in via REDWOOD_ALLOW_UNSIGNED=1 for legacy flows, but this will produce deprecation logs. Well share migration playbooks.
kenji: How will this affect CDN mirrors and our public registries?
maya: No CDN changes. Signed artifacts are uploaded to the same buckets and mirrored. Docs pages will show a short "Provenance" card linking to the SBOM and the signature fingerprint for the sample shown.
maya: Example developer flow:
```
# download release, verify signature, install
curl -O https://artifacts.redwood.com/redwood-sdk-4.3.0.whl
redwood-sig verify redwood-sdk-4.3.0.whl --pub-key ~/.redwood/pub.pem
pip install redwood-sdk-4.3.0.whl
```
kenji: Who needs to review the customer notice? CS/Support?
maya: Yes  CS will get a KB draft. Well send an enterprise notice two weeks before enforcement and a general notice one month prior.
jason: Anything for SDK maintainers?
maya: Maintainers must sign CI artifacts before publish. Well add signing steps to the release GitHub Actions and a local helper CLI for manual publishes.
olivia-k: :thumbsup: thanks, looks reasonable.
maya: Ill drop the RFC + a short internal blog post in #docs. Ping me if you want to review wording for customers. Thanks!
